title: What can you say about green tea extract in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for green tea extract; the strongest is "Provides antioxidants that help protect cells against free radical damage" (moderate, up to 690 mg total catechins a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Prevents breast or prostate cancer, outside FDA's qualified wording".

supported_wordings.wording: Provides antioxidants that help protect cells against free radical damage.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at up to 690 mg of total catechins a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: up to 690 mg total catechins a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: not more than 690 mg of total catechins a day, including at most 300 mg EGCG and at most 150 mg caffeine; take with food; ask a health care practitioner for use beyond 12 weeks.
supported_wordings.form: Standardized green tea leaf extract (Camellia sinensis), counted as catechins, EGCG and caffeine

sources.name: Health Canada monograph: Green Tea Extract

supported_wordings.wording: Used with a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity, helps in weight management.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 136-300 mg EGCG with 75-150 mg caffeine a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: 136-300 mg EGCG and 75-150 mg caffeine a day, at an EGCG to caffeine ratio of 1.8:1 to 4:1, and not more than 690 mg of total catechins; take with food; ask a health care practitioner for use beyond 12 weeks.
supported_wordings.form: Standardized green tea leaf extract (Camellia sinensis), counted as catechins, EGCG and caffeine

sources.name: Health Canada monograph: Green Tea Extract

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Prevents breast or prostate cancer, outside FDA's qualified wording
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names cancer. FDA's qualified claim on green tea and these cancers has set wording (see fda_health_claims).

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Works like a prescription weight-loss drug
wordings_to_avoid.why: Presents the product as a drug.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
